# omada_switch (Resource)

General configuration of an existing Omada-managed switch, currently its name. The switch must already be adopted by the controller: creating this resource takes over the adopted switch, and removing it only stops Terraform management; it does not forget or reset the switch. Both regular and Agile Series (Easy Managed) switches are supported.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Manages the name of a switch the controller has already adopted. It does not
# adopt or forget a switch: removing this resource only stops Terraform
# management. Regular and Agile Series (Easy Managed) switches both work.
resource "omada_switch" "core" {
  mac  = "AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF"
  name = "core-switch"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mac` (String) MAC address of the adopted switch, using either colon or dash separators.
- `name` (String) Device name shown by the controller, 1 to 128 characters. Agile Series (Easy Managed) switches accept at most 32 characters.

### Optional

- `site_id` (String) Site ID. Defaults to the provider site.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Switches are imported by MAC address, which selects the switch on the
# provider's site. Use the controller's dash-separated MAC form.
terraform import omada_switch.core AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF

# A switch on another site is imported as "<site>:<switch_mac>", where <site>
# is either the site ID or the site name.
terraform import omada_switch.core Default:AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF
```
